samples.text: The period is being carried by a manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That override rests on one confirmed finding, which is that the fault is a stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Engineers corrected the affected codes by hand, so the valuation could finish without waiting for a permanent fix to the register. The override is a stopgap. It covers this period only, and it depends on the engineers who applied it. For readers deciding whether to wait, the position is provisional but stable. The override is enough to let the period proceed, and nothing in the evidence so far suggests that it has introduced a new error. It does not change how the mapping is maintained, and the mapping is still kept by hand, so the next code change can break the join again. Teams that need final figures can use the current output for the period. Teams that plan around future runs should not assume the problem

The valuation run for the period failed because of a stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. That is the confirmed cause, and it sits in reference data, not in compute, storage or the network. The register paired legacy codes with cloud codes that no longer matched, so the join between the two returned nothing the valuation could use. Before it was found, the working theory was an overnight ERP outage. That theory was the first explanation the team logged, and it no longer stands. It fell away once engineers checked the upstream source directly and established that ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. Behind the stale mapping sits a weaker control. The review classifies the root cause as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer, so no one was obliged to look at the table when agency codes changed.
